title: Repeating Shape Patterns Worksheets for Kindergarten
intro: Teach repeating patterns by identifying the whole repeating unit.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Circle the first group of three shapes and compare it with the next group. Have the student repeat the unit aloud before drawing.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Read this group aloud: circle, circle, triangle. Repeat it: circle, circle, triangle. After those two complete groups, the next shape is a circle because a new copy of the group begins.

The other pattern on these pages repeats circle, triangle, square. After a circle and triangle at the end of a row, the square completes that group. Always check where the row stops before choosing the next shape.

Ask your student

Which shape comes next within the repeating group?

If your student needs help

If the student copies only the last shape, return to the complete three-shape unit.
